Subject: Recap & next steps: Performance SLOs (p95/p99) — hosted vs current provider

Hi Carlos,

Thanks for the call today — great to meet the FinLytics team. Quick recap and proposed next steps focused on performance targets so we can validate fit for Redwood Hosted API vs your current provider.

Recap:
- Primary workloads: real-time scoring for customer-facing product (single-turn prompt generation + light context lookups)
- Current provider: proprietary endpoint with average payload ~600 tokens, batching disabled for lowest latency
- Key perf goals: end-to-end p95 <= 220ms, p99 <= 420ms for single-request path; burst concurrency up to 250 QPS; streaming required for progressive token delivery for long responses (>1k tokens expected in some flows).
- Observations from call: you currently see p95 ~270ms and p99 ~500ms on peak; willing to trade slight increase in p95 for better cost predictability but p99 cannot exceed 500ms consistently.

Proposed next steps:
1) Please confirm the traffic profile (tokens per request distribution, average tokens) and peak concurrency window.
2) We'll run an internal qualification run against Redwood Hosted (non-production) to measure end-to-end p95/p99 with your sample prompts — requires a short NDA + signing of test account (I can share link).
3) I’ll loop in Aditya (runtime engineering) and Rishi (solutions) to discuss streaming and cache strategies if the initial numbers look promising.

Attached: SLO-matrix.xlsx (proposed measurement matrix) and a short runbook for the test.

If that works, I’ll schedule the run for next Tue/Wed and share a HubSpot link with the test account details.

Best,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: Performance SLOs (p95/p99) — hosted vs current provider

Thanks Marissa — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side before we hand files over for a run: 

- Token distribution: our median is ~420 tokens, 75th percentile ~650, 95th ~1,100 (the long flows you mentioned).
- Traffic shape: steady-state ~70 QPS, 99th percentile bursts up to ~260 QPS for short windows (1-3 minutes).
- Streaming: we use progressive streaming today for customer chat flows; full finalization latency is less important than first-byte latency for UX.

Quick Qs:
1) For the Hosted test, will you be able to replicate the burst pattern (250 QPS) or do you need a staged ramp?
2) How are you measuring end-to-end p95/p99 — is this client-observed (including network) or server-side? We need client-observed to match what we see in prod.
3) Any compatibility concerns with our current authentication/headers?

We can sign the test NDA and deliver a sample payload set and a small harness if you share the DocSend link again.

Carlos
Carlos Ramirez
Head of Platform
FinLytics
c.ramirez@finlytics.com

Great context — thanks Carlos. Short answers inline: 

1) We can replicate burst patterns in our non-prod harness. We typically run both a staged ramp and a peak blast to capture warmup effects. For your case we’ll do: 0->70 QPS ramp over 2 min, hold 3 min, then 0->260 QPS burst for 2 min, repeat 3 cycles.

2) We'll report both server-side and client-observed numbers. For parity with your production numbers, we'll prioritize client-observed p95/p99 (we run the client harness from a colocated test agent to mimic your network). Please confirm if you'd like tests from a specific region (us-east/us-west/eu).

3) Authentication: Redwood Hosted supports standard bearer tokens and can accept custom headers — no breaking changes expected. If you have a custom HMAC header today, send the spec and we’ll wire it into the test harness.

I’ve shared the DocSend NDA link here: https://docsend.com/view/finlytics-nda and will attach the test run instructions to the HubSpot ticket. If you can drop the sample payloads (anonymized) by EOD Wed we'll aim for a Thurs or next Tue run.

Also looping in Aditya R. and Rishi M. to confirm runtime-level expectations (streaming first-byte, KV caching options, and concurrency tuning).

Best,
Marissa

Team — forwarding the FinLytics thread. Key asks:
- Client-observed p95 target: <=220ms, p99 <=420ms for single-request path.
- Burst concurrency: replicate up to 260 QPS during test. Steady-state ~70 QPS.
- Streaming: prioritize first-byte latency for long responses; they will rely on progressive delivery.
- Payloads: median ~420 tokens, 95th ~1,100 tokens.

Can we provision a non-prod Hosted endpoint and a test harness to run their burst pattern? Please confirm:
1) Which model variant to use for the test (recommendation: quantized 8-bit variant with streaming enabled).
2) Any runtime flags to tune KV cache + batching to favor low p95 (we may need to disable some batching for the single-request path).
3) Expected client-observed delta vs server-side (ballpark).

Internal notes (for your context): Redwood usually sees ~p95 180-240ms and p99 350-480ms for similar single-turn workloads on hosted depending on region and model. We'll need to show they meet their p99 ceiling of 500ms — ideally <420ms.

Thanks — cc'ing Rishi for solutions patterns (streaming + cache). Marissa
